title: Why Christians and Jews refuse images
source_text: Ὥσπερ οὖν τὸ ἓν τοῦτο πρᾶγμα, ἡ τῆς μοιχείας ἀποχὴ, ἓν εἶναι δοκοῦσα πολλὰ ἁλίσκεται τυγχάνουσα παρὰ τὰ διάφορα δόγματα καὶ τὰς προθέσεις, οὕτως καὶ τῶν μὴ ἀνεχομένων παρὰ βωμοῖς καὶ ναοῖς καὶ ἀγάλμασι σέβειν τὸ θεῖον Σκύθαι μὲν ἢ Λιβύων οἱ Νομάδες ἢ Σῆρες οἱ ἄθεοι ἢ Πέρσαι ἀπὸ δογμάτων τοῦτο πράττουσιν ἄλλων, ἢ ὧν Χριστιανοὶ καὶ Ἰουδαῖοι οὐκ ἀνέχονται τῆς τοιαύτης ὑπολαμβανομένης εἰς τὸ θεῖον θεραπείας· οὐδεὶς ἐκείνων διὰ τὸ ἐκκλίνειν καὶ κατασπᾶν καὶ κατάγειν τὴν περὶ τὸ θεῖον θρησκείαν ἐπὶ τὴν τοιαύτην ὕλην οὑτωσὶ ἐσχηματισμένην οὐκ ἀνέχεται βωμῶν καὶ ἀγαλμάτων οὐδὲ διὰ τὸ διειληφέναι περὶ δαιμόνων ὅτι τοιοῖσδε παρακαθέζονται σχήμασι καὶ χωρίοις, ἤτοι ὑπό τινων μαγγανειῶν κατακλιθέντες ἢ καὶ ἄλλως δυνηθέντες προκαταλαβεῖν ἑαυτοῖς τόπους, ἐν οἷς τῆς τῶν θυομένων ἀποφορᾶς λίχνως μεταλαμβάνοντες παράνομον ἡδονὴν καὶ παρανόμους θηράσονται· Χριστιανοὶ δὲ καὶ Ἰουδαῖοι διὰ τὸ „κύριον τὸν θεόν σου φοβηθήσῃ καὶ αὐτῷ μόνῳ λατρεύσεις“ (καὶ) διὰ τὸ „οὐκ ἔσονταί σοι θεοὶ ἕτεροι πλὴν ἐμοῦ“ καὶ „οὐ ποιήσεις σεαυτῷ εἴδωλον οὐδὲ παντὸς ὁμοίωμα, ὅσα ἐν τῷ οὐρανῷ (ἄνω) καὶ ὅσα ἐν τῇ γῇ κάτω καὶ ὅσα ἐν τῷ ὕδατι ὑποκάτω τῆς γῆς· οὐ προσκυνήσεις αὐτοῖς οὐδὲ μὴ λατρεύσεις αὐτοῖς“ καὶ διὰ τὸ „κύριον τὸν θεόν σου προσκυνήσεις καὶ αὐτῷ μόνῳ λατρεύσεις“ καὶ ἄλλα πλείονα τούτοις παραπλήσια οὐ μόνον ἐκτρέπονται νεὼς καὶ βωμοὺς καὶ ἀγάλματα, ἀλλὰ καὶ ἐπὶ τὸ ἀποθνῄσκειν, ὅτε δεῖ, ἑτοίμως ἔρχονται ὑπὲρ τοῦ μὴ μολῦναι τὴν περὶ τοῦ θεοῦ τῶν ὅλων ὑπόληψιν διά τινος τοιούτου παρανομήματος.
pass_a_gloss: Just as (ὥσπερ) then this one thing/matter (πρᾶγμα), the abstention (ἀποχή) from adultery (μοιχεία), seeming (δοκέω) to be one, is caught/found (ἁλίσκομαι) being many according to the different doctrines (δόγματα) and purposes/intentions (προθέσεις), so also of those not tolerating (ἀνέχομαι) to revere (σέβω) the divine (τὸ θεῖον) at altars (βωμοί) and temples (ναοί) and images (ἀγάλματα): Scythians, or the Nomads of the Libyans, or the Seres the godless (ἄθεοι), or Persians do this from other doctrines than those from which Christians and Jews do not tolerate such supposed (ὑπολαμβανομένη) service (θεραπεία) toward the divine. None of those, on account of shunning (ἐκκλίνω) and dragging down (κατασπάω) and bringing down (κατάγω) the religion/worship (θρησκεία) concerning the divine onto such matter (ὕλη) thus shaped (σχηματίζω), does not tolerate altars and images; nor on account of having discerned (διαλαμβάνω) about demons (δαίμονες) that they sit beside (παρακαθέζομαι) such shapes (σχήματα) and places (χωρία), either made to lodge/installed (κατακλίνω) by certain sorceries (μαγγανεῖαι) or in some other way able to seize beforehand (προκαταλαμβάνω) places for themselves, in which, greedily (λίχνως) partaking (μεταλαμβάνω) of the exhalation/fumes (ἀποφορά) of the things sacrificed (θύω), they will hunt (θηράω) lawless (παράνομος) pleasure (ἡδονή) and lawless [men]. But Christians and Jews, on account of 'the Lord your God you shall fear and him alone you shall serve (λατρεύω)' and on account of 'there shall not be to you other gods besides me' and 'you shall not make for yourself an idol (εἴδωλον) nor a likeness (ὁμοίωμα) of anything, whatever is in heaven above and whatever in the earth below and whatever in the water beneath the earth; you shall not bow down (προσκυνέω) to them nor serve them' and on account of 'the Lord your God you shall worship (προσκυνέω) and him alone you shall serve' and many others similar to these, not only turn away from (ἐκτρέπομαι) temples and altars and images, but also come readily (ἑτοίμως) to dying (ἀποθνῄσκω), when it is necessary (δεῖ), for the sake of not defiling (μολύνω) the conception (ὑπόληψις) about the God of the universe (ὁ θεὸς τῶν ὅλων) by some such transgression (παρανόμημα).
pass_b_english: Just as this one act, abstaining from adultery, seems to be one thing yet is found to be many, according to the different doctrines and intentions behind it, so it is with those who will not tolerate worshipping the divine at altars, temples and images. The Scythians, the nomads of Libya, the godless Seres and the Persians do this from doctrines other than those from which Christians and Jews will not tolerate what is taken to be such service of the divine. None of those peoples refuses to tolerate altars and images because he shrinks from dragging down and lowering the worship of the divine to matter shaped in this way; nor because he has come to understand that demons haunt such shapes and places, either installed there by certain sorceries or able in some other way to seize places for themselves beforehand, where, greedily partaking of the fumes of the sacrifices, they will hunt after lawless pleasure and lawless men.

Christians and Jews, by contrast, act because of the words, “You shall fear the Lord your God, and him only shall you serve” (Deuteronomy 6:13), and “You shall have no other gods besides me” (Exodus 20:3; Deuteronomy 5:7), and “You shall not make for yourself an idol, nor a likeness of anything that is in heaven above, or that is in the earth beneath, or that is in the water under the earth; you shall not bow down to them, nor serve them” (Exodus 20:4–5), and again, “You shall worship the Lord your God, and him only shall you serve” (Matthew 4:10; Luke 4:8), and many other sayings like these. Because of them they not only turn away from temples, altars and images, but go readily even to death, when they must, so as not to defile by any such transgression the conception they hold of the God of the universe.

choices.choice: Continues the comparison begun in 7.63 (abstaining from adultery for different reasons). ‘The godless Seres’ repeats Celsus’s own label (Σῆρες οἱ ἄθεοι, 7.62); Origen reports it, it is not his own judgement. The Seres are the far-eastern people the Greeks knew through the silk trade; the name is kept. The clause διὰ τὸ ἐκκλίνειν καὶ κατασπᾶν καὶ κατάγειν τὴν ... θρησκείαν is awkward as transmitted (three coordinate infinitives governing one object); rendered by sense, ‘because he shrinks from dragging down and lowering the worship’, and the double negative οὐδεὶς ... οὐκ ἀνέχεται resolved as ‘none ... refuses to tolerate’. κατακλιθέντες (‘made to lodge, installed’) anticipates the κατακλίσεις, rites of installation, of 7.69. ἀποφορά: the exhalation or reek of the sacrifices. παρανόμους θηράσονται: Koetschau’s text, read as ‘lawless men’ (masculine object). Deuteronomy 6:13: Origen’s wording (φοβηθήσῃ ... αὐτῷ μόνῳ λατρεύσεις) matches the LXX in Codex Alexandrinus, which adds μόνῳ (‘only’). The final quotation, with προσκυνήσεις (‘worship’), is Jesus’s form of the same verse in Matthew 4:10 and Luke 4:8. Exodus 20:4–5 follows the LXX (‘in the water under the earth’), parallel Deuteronomy 5:8–9.
